sections.title: Questions keep the same shape
sections.content: A question with fog + infinitive doesn't change the word order you already use in a statement — a question word like mit just takes the spot right in front of fog, and a yes/no question uses the exact same order as a statement, marked only by the question mark (and, out loud, by intonation).

items.english: What will you do this weekend?
Will you (pl.) help Gábor in the house?

sections.content: For a yes/no question you can also front fog itself for a more pointed, "well, will you..." feel — Fogsz segíteni? — but Segíteni fogsz? with plain rising intonation works just as well. Either way, the infinitive at the end never moves.

sections.title: A prefixed infinitive in a plain statement
sections.content: With a prefixed verb like felújít, the prefix jumps in front of fog itself in a neutral statement: Fel fogunk újítani egy szobát ("We will renovate a room"), not Fogunk felújítani. Keep this in mind for the next lesson's look at questions and nem.
